subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & next steps for Acme Logistics MAP POC
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@acme.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & Mutual Action Plan — Acme Logistics MAP POC

Hi Sam —

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking us through the current routing and cost pain points. Per our conversation, here’s a short recap and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) to keep momentum for the POC.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Spikes in inference cost during peak scheduling windows (3–5x baseline).
- Occasional tail-latency affecting route optimization jobs (SLO goal 200ms).
- Internal compliance requirement: audit logs and data residency for routing metadata.

Goals for the POC:
1) Validate Redwood’s cost-per-token improvements and 30–40% cost reduction with batching + caching for routing workloads.
2) Demonstrate stable median latency < 120ms and 99th percentile < 300ms under expected load.
3) Provide evidence for audit/logging integration and an implementation plan for private deployment if needed.

Mutual Action Plan (proposed):
- Milestone 1 — POC kickoff: define success metrics and access (week of Jul 6) — Owner: Sam / Acme; Target: 2026-07-08
- Milestone 2 — Baseline collection: run 1 week of traffic with instrumentation (Jul 9–16) — Owner: Acme + Redwood SE (Dylan); Target: 2026-07-16
- Milestone 3 — Redwood tuning & config: batching, cache profiles, quantization recommendations (Jul 17–24) — Owner: Redwood (Mateo/Dylan); Target: 2026-07-24
- Milestone 4 — Validation & demo: cost/latency comparison and security signoff (Jul 27–31) — Owner: Joint; Target: 2026-07-31
- Milestone 5 — Procurement & contract review: finalize SOW and terms (by Aug 12) — Owner: Acme procurement + Redwood sales; Target: 2026-08-12

Open questions / dependencies:
- Which Acme environments can we get read-only telemetry from for baseline collection?
- Will procurement provide a standard MSA or should we route via Redwood’s SOW + procurement redlines?
- Who needs to be involved from Acme security to validate audit log format?

Attachments: MAP_Acme-Logistics_v1.xlsx (draft MAP with milestones and acceptance criteria).

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the POC kickoff week (Jul 6 or Jul 13)?
- Please add any missing stakeholders (procurement, security) so we can include them in the MAP.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

---
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference for products

Thanks, Sam — this is helpful. I've updated the MAP to include explicit acceptance criteria for latency and a short SOW draft attached (Redwood_SOW_Draft.pdf).

Updated acceptance criteria (added to MAP):
- Median inference latency <= 120ms for the routing model under target traffic profile.
- 99th percentile latency <= 300ms.
- Cost reduction: >= 30% improvement in cost-per-inference compared to current baseline with no batching.
- Audit logs: show end-to-end request/response IDs and delivery timestamps for 7 days retention (or longer per procurement needs).

Action items from Redwood:
- Mateo/Dylan: coordinate with Acme infra to confirm telemetry endpoint and sample rate (by Jul 6).
- Marissa: share updated MAP and SOW with procurement/legal for early review (by Jul 6).

Attaching: Redwood_SOW_Draft.pdf and updated MAP_Acme-Logistics_v1.xlsx.

If we can get procurement's MSA by Jul 6 as you suggested, we'll plan to route Redwood's SOW + redlines to accelerate review.

Best,
Marissa

Internal note — tagging for transparency.

Dylan / Marissa — proposed technical POC scope details for Redwood SE work:
- Collect 72 hours of representative routing requests (sample rate 10%) to build KV-cache and sequence length distribution.
- Run baseline inference on current model (on Acme infra read-only endpoint) to capture median/99th latency and token counts.
- Test three config profiles: (1) standard batching, (2) prefix caching enabled, (3) quantized variant + caching.
- Deliverable: short report with cost/latency delta by profile + config repo and runbook.

I'll draft the runbook sections for instrumentation and share by EOD Jul 6.
